messages:
mike: quick heads-up — after the 11:15 deploy i'm seeing ~6% drop in prefix cache hit rate for long-tail seqs (>512) on prod-gpu-pool-2. evictions are up and the KV store shows lots of small fragments. can someone run a short sampling profile + sanity check on compaction config?

alyssa: on it. grabbing a live snapshot now. which route/model?

mike: route: /v1/generate, model: xlarge-v2-prod, model_id: mdl-2026-04-17. i can paste the minimal logs i pulled.

mike: ```
PREFIXCACHE: node=node7 pool=prod-gpu-pool-2 hit_rate=0.782 -> 0.723 delta=-0.059
KV_METRICS: fragments=48932 prev=16210 compaction_runs=42
EVICTIONS: 5m_rate=0.24/s -> 1.1/s
```

raj: last week i landed a tweak to compaction heuristics (lowered min_fragment_threshold). could be related. what was the pre-deploy compaction config?

mike: before: `min_frag_size=64`, `compact_on_write=true`. after deploy i think the binary flipped `min_frag_size=32` in the new default. travis had a diff: https://git.redwood/infra/kv/commit/9a4f2

taylor: if compaction is too eager it can create many small free slots that increase fragmentation paradoxically. also can increase eviction churn because slots are fragmented. would like to see prefix length distribution and free-slot histogram.

alyssa: snapshot pulled. running `kv-inspect --node node7 --hist prefix_len --buckets 16` now, should have results in ~6m.

jeff: fwiw node7 recovered from a soft OOM yesterday (killed a worker and restarted), so some cold-cache effects are expected. but 6% sustained hit drop seems more than warmup noise.

natalie: can we run a controlled compare: current (prod) vs rollback to old compaction flags on a canary? i can spin a two-node canary run with `prefixcache-sim` workload.

li: i'll do the canary toggle. plan: fork config, set `min_frag_size=64`, `compact_on_write=false` on canary nodes node10/11, replay 1h of sampled requests (long-tail seed). will post metrics. give me ~20m. :eyes:

mike: thanks li! if possible, also grab `kv_fragment_map | wc -l` and `cat /proc/kv/free_slots | head -n 40` so we can see slot granularity.

perf-bot: generated flamegraph (canary-run-1908765432) -> https://perf.redwood/graphs/fg-1908765432.html :chart_with_upwards_trend:

alyssa: hist output (trimmed):
```
prefix_len_buckets: [0-64]: 12.3% [64-256]: 34.1% [256-512]: 18.7% [512-1024]: 25.6% [1024+]: 9.3%
free_slot_sizes: small(<64)=41230 medium(64-256)=7100 large(>256)=602
```

taylor: that free_slot_sizes number is suspicious — tiny slots are dominating. matches the compaction hypothesis.

raj: quick thought — our compaction path coalesces adjacent freed slots only if both are >= min_frag_size. lowering min_frag_size can actually break coalescing in some codepaths because it creates more smaller boundaries.

jeff: also check GC/allocator settings in the runtime; if mem allocs changed, fragmentation pattern in userspace can trickle down. any changes in the same deploy?

mike: looking at deploy diff now: only infra/kv and a tiny unrelated logging tweak. i'll attach the exact diff in a sec.

ops-bot: scheduled: rolling restart prod-gpu-pool-2 nodes 7-9 @ 2026-04-17T23:45:00Z (non-disruptive) :wrench:

natalie: can we avoid rolling restart until canary results? restarts will reset the experiment.

ops-bot: noted, action deferred.

li: canary run done. numbers:
```
canary (old config): hit_rate=0.778 evictions=0.18/s fragments=16512
prod (current): hit_rate=0.722 evictions=1.03/s fragments=48932
delta: hit +5.6% fragments -66% evictions -82%
```

mike: wow ok that's pretty conclusive. turning off eager compaction on prod should heal things.

taylor: agreed. propose a rollback of compaction defaults and then a gradual re-eval of compact heuristics with a regression harness. also add a unit test that asserts coalescing behavior for small fragments.

raj: i'll open a PR to revert the default and add the test. tagging for review @alyssa @jeff.

alyssa: ack, will review.

mike: thanks everyone. i'll coordinate a short deploy window to flip back the default and monitor hit-rate + eviction. post-mortem will include checklist to run `kv-inspect` after compaction changes. :thumbsup:

jeff: if you want, I can run a quick pre/post smoke script to compute moving-window hit-rate every 5m and wake us if it drifts more than 2%.
